verdict.rationale: Clerk documents a first-party Next.js integration and a CLI that detects your framework and adds the needed auth files. It also issues short-lived JWT session tokens for authenticating backend requests, and a community member praises the Next.js integration. But the pack never mentions middleware, route protection, edge-runtime verification, or SDKs for other frameworks. Missing for 10: documented middleware-based route protection, edge session verification, SDKs for peer frameworks beyond Next.js, and hands-on corroboration of route gating.

support.subject: As a developer, I can protect routes with first-party framework SDKs and middleware (Next.js and peers) that verify sessions at the edge

citations.quote: Easily add secure, beautiful, and fast authentication to Next.js with Clerk.
Clerk detects the framework, links an app, and adds the auth files your project needs.
Clerk generates a short-lived session token that you can use to authenticate requests to your backend.
The Next.js integration story is already really quite good
